analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/developer/build.md (date bump plus a new paragraph at head lines 204-207 on the optimized release cache also holding the native cluster worker build scratch directory) and docs/developer/test.md (date bump, sharded SDK 27 release qualification description, a new test script entry for scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, and cluster runtime registration-body tests). No source, workflow, or script changes are in the supplied units, so no runtime control is altered by this diff.

Security-relevant claims examined against the threat model. The release cache text states the worker's Metal library is deleted on restore and the JACCL/macOS 26.2 checks run on every build. That is consistent with the existing statement that cache restores never waive resource verification (T-054, A-017). The sharded qualification text states that signing requires qualify-sdk (which audits per-shard executed counts) plus optimized compilation, and that cache hits never skip tests. These are documented claims and do not weaken the stated gates. The cluster runtime registration notes cover a 64 KiB body limit, malformed-block refusal, and derived ID length limits, and say the facts step runs after final hashes with no secret and the keychain removed first. These are descriptive of existing and pending release plumbing (A-011, A-017, TB-011 related).

Unverified contract: the actual workflows and scripts (cache action, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, release pipeline, provider-test-shards.py) are not in the supplied evidence, so the accuracy of these documented claims, particularly that the cluster worker scratch directory cached in the optimized lane cannot carry stale or poisoned objects into a signed release, cannot be verified here. A reviewer of the accompanying code change should confirm cache key separation, the keychain removal ordering and that no secret is exposed to the facts step. No finding is raised because docs alone do not create a regression.
